display.purpose: The page title in the hero; the only h1.

headline.purpose: Chapter titles, as sentences ending in a full stop.

manifesto.purpose: One scrubbed statement per page; never below 28px.

title.purpose: Card, door, step and placard titles.

lead.purpose: The paragraph under a hero or chapter title.

body.purpose: Reading text, about 42rem wide at most.

label.purpose: Uppercase mono metadata: eyebrows, dates, table heads.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The hand-off sheet laid over the hero; the only structural shadow.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single high-intent action in a view, with its arrow in a disc.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 6px 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #ecd8b7; color: #140302; font: 600 14px/1 'General Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #fff5e6; } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-btn-disc { transform: translateX(2px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #140302, 0 0 0 4px #ecd8b7; } .ds-btn-disc { display: inline-flex; width: 32px; height: 32px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(20, 3, 2, 0.12); transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); }

narrative.overview:
The site reads like the programme a delegate is handed at the door of a formal event: index numerals, hairline rules, mono labels in small capitals, large confident headings, and a lot of paper around them. It is set in maroon lacquer and champagne ink in the dark theme, and in cream stock with burnt-sienna ink in the light theme. Both themes are first-class; every token is declared for each.

Pages are told as chapters. A hero sits still while the first chapter slides over it like a sheet laid on a desk; later chapters change ground (deep, crest, inverse paper) instead of adding boxes. Motion is the page being handled, never decoration: lines rise out of masks, sheets settle, rules draw themselves, numbers count to real values, and the curtain closes between pages. Everything that moves has a static reading that is complete on its own.

Two tracks share the system and never share a colour. Crimson belongs to GIMUN, champagne to the GIKI Moot Court. A colour on screen always tells you which room you are in.
keyCharacteristics: Chapters with grounds (deep, crest, inverse) rather than stacked cards.
Hairline rules and index numerals (01, 02) carry structure.
Mono labels for metadata only; headings are never set in mono.
One hero moment per page, one pinned or scrubbed sequence at most.
Nothing invented: every number, date and name comes from content.

rules.name: The Two Rooms Rule
rules.body: Crimson means GIMUN and champagne means GMC. Never use either as general decoration, and never put both on one control.

rules.name: The Tone Contract Rule
rules.body: A tone re-declares the ink tokens for its subtree. Inside .tone-deep, .tone-crest or .tone-inverse, use the ordinary text and line utilities; never hand-pick a colour for a tone. tests/unit/tone-contrast.test.ts holds every text token above 4.5:1 on every ground.

rules.name: The Full Stop Rule
rules.body: Display and chapter titles are sentences and end with a full stop ("The resource library."). One accent phrase per title may take the track or champagne colour.

rules.name: The No Em Dash Rule
rules.body: Copy never uses the em dash. Use a colon, a comma or a new sentence.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A new level is a new ground (tone) or a sheet, never a heavier drop shadow.

dos: Do let the h1 render with the page: load entrances are CSS transform-only, and no JS animation runs before the visitor's first scroll, tap or key.
Do give every scroll effect a complete static reading for reduced motion and for print.
Do use index numerals (01, 02, 03) and hairlines to show order and structure.
Do keep numbers real: counters, seats and dates come from content, never placeholders.
Do check both themes and both 390px and 1440px for every new surface.
donts: Don't use a thick coloured side border on cards.
Don't use bounce or overshoot easing; use the brand, expo, lift or curtain curves.
Don't set headings in mono, or body text in the display face.
Don't use crimson or champagne as decoration outside their track.
Don't add a second pinned or scrubbed sequence to a page that already has one.
